title: FROM THE THRONE TO THE MILLSTONE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Every firstborn son in Egypt will die, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who
sits on the throne, to the firstborn son of the female slave, who is at her hand
mill, and all the firstborn of the cattle as well." - Ex 11:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a heavy verse, and we should not rush past it or soften it. The
firstborn of Egypt would die, from the palace to the slave quarters.

Why the firstborn? In Egypt, the firstborn son carried the family's future, its
name, its inheritance. Pharaoh himself was worshipped as divine, and his
firstborn was the next god-king. This judgment struck at the heart of Egypt's
religion and Egypt's hope. It also answered something Egypt had done: Pharaoh
had ordered Israel's baby boys drowned in the Nile (Ex 1:22). Egypt had spent
generations killing other people's sons.

We should feel the weight of this. God's judgment is real, and sin against the
helpless is not overlooked. At the same time, notice that no Egyptian family
needed to die. The doorpost of any home marked with blood would be passed over
(Ex 12:13). The way of escape was open to all, and Ex 12:38 tells us many
non-Israelites did leave with them.

Here we see the shadow of the Gospel. God's judgment is real, and so is His
provision. The Father did not spare His own firstborn Son so that we could be
spared (Rom 8:32). The judgment we deserved fell on Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the reality of God's judgment seriously?
2. Have you personally taken shelter under the blood of Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You did not spare Your own Son but gave Him for me. I
take shelter in Jesus alone. Amen.
